reviews.title: Very effective and works best at night when the rest of the house is very dark. Bugs like light.
reviews.body: This is not a magic product as it will NOT stop the source of your bugs but it will continue catching flying bugs as long as you've got them. Bugs are attracted to light so you won't see this too effective during the day. It does its best work at night when the lights are out as these have a bright blue light that attracts the bugs. We had a plant that gnats called home and grew a large family so we used these to capture all of the loose gnats while we removed the source. It took about a week but eventually they all disappeared. I got the 2 pack. Put one upstairs and one downstairs in dark rooms with little to no light at night. After a few days, both had at least 10-15 bugs each. After a week, they all disappeared. Highly recommend.

reviews.title: Works well, but not for phorid flies. Simple setup.
reviews.body: It definitely catches multiple types of flies of various sizes, but doesn't "attract" phorid flies, (aka scuttle flies, humpback flies, or coffin flies). While it has caught a couple, they aren't attracted to UV, but they sometimes seem to congregate near my windows during the day, if anything to inspect the area as they do not stay for long. It works, but not for everything. Setup was simple. Quality is decent. Good product. Brighter than I originally thought.If you want to get rid of phorid flies, the best way to remove them or prevent them from taking your home for residence would be to keep your apartment clean. Find any sitting water (fridge drip pan, bottom dishwasher trap). Remove trash often (get a smaller can), find any left out food that has been rotting (this includes onions or garlic on the counter thats left in a bag - from personal experience). Seal trash with a tie or clamp, clean litter boxes often, etc.

reviews.title: Worth it!
reviews.body: My husband and I have quite the collection of houseplants going on.  We recently had a huge unexpected surge of those little brown gnats that hang around plants and pelt you in the face, especially in our bathroom with a south facing window, which doubles as a houseplant retreat when they look like they need a little sunlight infusion.  We also have had a smaller, but still annoying, surge in our bedroom, which also has houseplants in it.  Yesterday I decided I’d had enough and bought what I originally thought was a totally bougie and unnecessary purchase, these little light traps.  Why would I spend almost $30 on two little plugins when there are so many alternatives?BECAUSE:-These are nowhere near as hideous and gross looking as regular fly traps.  You do not see the flies until you remove them and they are small and sleek looking.-They attract the bugs with light, so I don’t have to just hope that the bugs wander into the trap.-They are chemical free which is important to me with an extremely curious toddler in the house.  We also tried home remedies like soapy water and apple cider vinegar to no avail, just a stanky vinegary bathroom, these have no smell and actually work.-They are super easy to install, you just peel the backing off the card, slide it into the unit, plug it in and let it do its thing.-It’s silent, you’re only aware of it because of the light, which my husband didn’t love, but he doesn’t love gnats pelting him in the face more, so we’ll take it.-It is super easy to clean and dispose of, it’s not unruly like regular fly traps.I didn’t want to spend money on this initially and put it off till I couldn’t stand it anymore, I wish I had just bought them earlier.  They are amazing.I’ve seen some complaints about these not treating the root cause of the problem/gnats and flies coming back.  Obviously, these won’t kill eggs or prevent other bugs from coming into your house.  But blaming the product for that is like buying a treadmill and then complaining that though it did help you exercise and did exactly what it said it would do, it didn’t stop you from overeating your favorite junk foods.  This does exactly what it’s supposed to do.  These photos are from one night, less than 12 hours, the difference is noticeable in our house.  We assumed it would be more effective at night because it’s the only light source attracting the bugs.  This may be my favorite purchase of 2024.My only complaint is that there is some kind of residue on the plug in itself which smears the printed on label, is a bit sticky and left black fingerprints around(last picture).  It came off when I washed my hands but this was annoying.  This happened before we even touched the sticky paper, so we know it’s an issue with the actual plugin unit.  Still worth it to us.

reviews.title: I'm a believer!!
reviews.body: I was skeptical but, given the reviews and frustration with the knats in our house, gave this product a try.  I plugged one of them in around 6pm when I got home from work.  I checked the trap about 11PM before going to bed.  There were 16 knats stuck on the trap.  I checked again the next morning and the count was up to 37.  The trap is plugged in a kitchen counter outlet.  We have a lot of house plants and I think that is the source of the problem.  We keep the house "not lived in" clean.  Next step is a 1-to-4 parts peroxide to water mix for the plants.  I read this will kill any larvae in the plants without harming them.  So, a two prong approach.  Kill the adults and also try to find and treat the source.  There were no other insect types caught or that we see.  Just the knats.

reviews.body: I couldn’t be happier with these! Flying bugs are the bane of my existence and I’ve struggled to find an effective solution for years. Fly strips have been the best I could do until I finally stumbled upon these.Most importantly: they work. The morning after I plugged both in (one by the sink and the other by the plants), there were zero flying bugs in the house. ZERO. After years of tolerating flying pests in the kitchen and living room, the relief was palpable.That stillness lasted for about a week and a half before a couple of flies made their way in and seemed to survive the night. I’m not sure how long these would last in an environment with fewer flying pests to address, but I’m more than satisfied with the results.There are many sticky pads on Amazon that fit these fixtures which are cheap enough to make this purchase a no brainer.
